candidates.name: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
support_spans: dilated ducts with broad papillary structures, a mono- to multilayer epithelial covering, and densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei
ER 90%, PR 90%, HER2 negative, Ki-67 20%, CK5/6 negative, E-cadherin positive, p63 negative, calponin negative, and GATA3 positive
candidates.why: The presence of dilated ducts, atypical nuclei, and specific immunohistochemistry results support this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Intraductal Papillary Carcinoma
support_spans: dilated ducts with broad papillary structures
fused papillary networks with abundant fibrovascular cores
candidates.why: The presence of papillary structures and fused papillary networks with abundant fibrovascular cores is characteristic of Intraductal Papillary Carcinoma.

candidates.name: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
support_spans: dilated ducts with broad papillary structures
densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei
candidates.why: The presence of dilated ducts with broad papillary structures and densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei is consistent with Ductal Carcinoma In Situ.

candidates.name: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
support_spans: a large irregular cystic-solid lesion with internal fluid levels and tortuous vessels
loss of normal architecture with mixed cystic (>90%) and solid echoes
candidates.why: The presence of a large irregular cystic-solid lesion with internal fluid levels and tortuous vessels, as well as the loss of normal architecture, is consistent with Invasive Ductal Carcinoma.

candidates.name: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
support_spans: dilated ducts with broad papillary structures, a mono- to multilayer epithelial covering, and densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei
candidates.why: The presence of densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei and the absence of myoepithelial markers support this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Intraductal Papillary Carcinoma
support_spans: broad papillary structures, a mono- to multilayer epithelial covering
candidates.why: The presence of broad papillary structures and a mono- to multilayer epithelial covering are characteristic of intraductal papillary carcinoma.

candidates.name: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
support_spans: dilated ducts
contradict_spans: densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei
candidates.why: While the presence of dilated ducts could suggest DCIS, the presence of densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei suggests invasive disease.

selector.rationale: The presence of a large irregular cystic-solid lesion with internal fluid levels and tortuous vessels, along with the absence of myoepithelial markers and the presence of fused papillary networks, supports Invasive Ductal Carcinoma. The immunohistochemistry results also align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
rejected.why: The presence of densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei contradicts Ductal Carcinoma In Situ.
